title: −13915*G DNA polymorphism associated with lactase persistence in Africa interacts with Oct-1
authors: Olds LC, Ahn JK, Sibley E
funder: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases grants DK60074 and DK60715.
result: Lactase persistence is autosomal dominant and correlated with SNPs about 14 kb upstream of LCT. In transfected cells the SNP-region DNA acts as a cis element that enhances lactase promoter activity; the -13907*G and -13910*T region sequences interact with the transcription factor Oct-1, and EMSA and supershift show that -13915*G does too. Oct-1 binding remains a candidate interaction in lactase persistence.
